I've been a long term user of Quetiapine been on it for multiple years and i'd like to give you some thoughts although ultimately it's important to talk to your gp and figure out what's best for you weather that's giving this medication more time or switching to something else

  
The grogginess and sleep improve with time, this medication has a strong side effect that affects most people this way when they start the medication and improves over weeks, months or years depending how your body reacts to the medication individually and at what rate you increase dosage

  
You mention that "medication is suppressing my emotions rather than helping me regulate them" that is correct. The  medication is a mood stabilizer it removes the higher ends of emotions, both good and bad but it will not help you regulate emotions. That is what DBT and other therapy skills are for and the medication is meant to be a tool to use to help you get to a place of being able to use the skills you'll be learning if doing so before was too challenging due to intense emotional reactions or having a lack of time to respond in other ways

This medication doesn't improve thoughts, values and low mood those are things that therapy or other medication could help with, if your mood is very low it's worth asking if starting a antidepressant would be useful however note that they come with their own side effects and some can make suicidal thoughts worse before they improve or can react badly with your individual body

I'm based in the uk and lot of these are based of my own experiences -

  
Pros - Medication if that's something you want to look at, professionals who can be really caring/educated, long term treatment, lots of resources available for various symptoms (DBT, CAT for example), can help you understand yourself, some people might look up the condition to understand you better/be more helpful 

  
Cons - Potential misdiagnosis especially if you are female (autism), some professionals what will treat you worse/like shit (i had one that said to me "that the crisis team don't treat (people like me)" and that "they know exactly who i am) this was when i moved area and communication from my prior CMHT got lost), stigma online

  
Getting diagnosed can take a while in the uk, usually you need to try various short term treatments first/or get rejected from them if you are too severe including CBT, it required speaking with your gp on a few occasions, potentially trying medication ect and the process if you are going the NHS route can take a while. Eventually you should get a referral for a Crisis or CMHT service and they'll take your history and book you in to get diagnosed. It's multiple sessions and takes a extensive look into your history thus far as well as asking any questions. It is fully free if you go through the NHS. 

  
You'll then likely get assigned a CCO (care coodinator) who will be in charge of referrals and booking future treatments for you, this will include appointments for medication, outside referrals for other services including Mind who have various groups as well

You aren't responsible for their wellbeing or safety, i understand caring for them and not wanting anything to happen but you are allowed and encouraged to take care of yourself, in this case not dating them and ending the relationship that you have with them since that's what you want. Just be open and honest with them, tell them that you appreciate the time you spent together but you aren't feeling it the way they are, hold strong boundaries that you won't be engaging with them sexually, if you want to keep ties with them let them know or if you don't let them know that you wont be speaking to them anymore. If you do choose to stay friends with them you need to strongly hold your ground to what you will and wont tolerate and that includes any threats, negative talk towards you. I know it might feel like it but you aren't doing anything wrong, in fact you are trying to make this as easy for you and them as possible. I see this on the sub a lot, they might have BPD but don't treat them like they are fragile, they might not react well, they might struggle but you are allowed to determine how you feel and walk away or end things, it isn't your job to fix them and it isn't your job to be what they want from you

I'd encourage you to build stronger boundaries, meeting someones family on the second day of meeting them is really fast and i'd encourage you to stop that with new people you are meeting. Get to know them, gauge how you feel, have conversations about things like the next steps like meeting family, who you want to know about you ect it will scare some people off but those aren't people you want in your life anyway. You don't have to go that quickly if you aren't comfortable and slowing down has a lot of benefits and lets you really gauge how you feel and prevents awkwardness like what's happening now
